hook_text: Some fossils are parts of an animal. Others are just the marks it left behind. Can you tell which is which?
clip_script: West Coast Fossil Park. Teeth, jaws and leg bones from ancient bears and sabre-toothed cats, five million years old. These are body fossils: real parts of living things, turned to stone. Now Langebaan Lagoon. Footprints of a person, pressed into wet sand about 117,000 years ago, now hard sandstone. That is a trace fossil: a sign left behind. Nests, eggs, burrows and droppings are trace fossils too!
visual_style: Whiteboard split screen: a body-fossil side with a tooth, bone, shell and leaf, and a trace-fossil side with footprints, a nest and a burrow.
mood: Detective-style curiosity with a satisfying sort.
pacing: Quick sort into two piles, then one clue from each.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort fossils like a palaeontologist.
